title: [Audit] 🔐 Identity & Access
description: Who authenticated, how, from where, and what failed. Resolves the numeric user.name into real identities.

config.content:
### Who signed in, how, and what failed

See which sign-in methods and credentials are in use, your busiest people and API keys, every key and when it was last used, and each failed or denied attempt.

Use it to check that access looks the way you expect, to review API keys, or to follow up on a run of failed sign-ins. Empty failure panels are good news.

**How to use it:** choose a Project, Person (email) or Client IP in the controls and set the time picker. Click an email in a table to filter the whole suite to that person.

config.description: Distinct identities in all traffic, resolved as email, then API key name, then user.name — one per row of Identity first and last seen. The people among them, by email, are the Humans tile beside it. The line under the number counts the API keys among them that have no email, by name (a Cloud API key, which has none, by its id): a re-issued key keeps its name, so it counts once here and once per id in the API keys tile. A key named after a person (syn-new-hire-…) is still a key. The rest of the number is service accounts and built-in users (elastic/kibana, autoscaling), user names tried in a failed sign-in (admin, elastic), and the placeholders for requests that presented no identity (<anonymous>, <unauthenticated-…>) — each a row in that session.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS BY user.email, api_key.name, user.name, user.domain | EVAL actor = COALESCE(user.email, api_key.name, user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS `Identities` = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor), keys = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor) WHERE user.email IS NULL AND (api_key.name IS NOT NULL OR user.domain == "_cloud_api_key") | EVAL detail = CASE(keys == 0, "no API keys", keys == 1, "incl. 1 key name", CONCAT("incl. ", CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) <= 3, TO_STRING(keys), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(keys), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(keys), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(keys), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(keys), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(keys), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(keys), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(keys), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(keys), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(keys), 3))), " key names")) | KEEP `Identities`, detail

config.description: Distinct email addresses in all traffic — the people Busiest human identities ranks. An Elasticsearch API key carries its creator's email, so a person can count here through a key they made without signing in; the line under the number says how many of them used SAML SSO in range (a browser session, whether it began in range or earlier — SSO events beside it says which).

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS `Humans` = COUNT_DISTINCT(user.email), sso = COUNT_DISTINCT(user.email) WHERE user.domain == "cloud-saml-kibana" | EVAL detail = CASE(sso == 0, "none used SSO", CONCAT(CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) <= 3, TO_STRING(sso), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(sso), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(sso), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(sso), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(sso), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(sso), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(sso), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(sso), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(sso), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(sso), 3))), " used SSO")) | KEEP `Humans`, detail

config.description: Distinct API keys seen in range, by id, of both kinds: Elastic Cloud API keys (recorded by id only) and Elasticsearch API keys (by id and name) — one per row of API key inventory. The line under the number counts the names those ids carry (a Cloud API key, which has none, by its id), one per row of Busiest API keys by name: a re-issued Elasticsearch key keeps its name under a new id, so a name with many ids is one key re-issued many times. These are the key names in the Identities tile beside it, unless a person created a key: that key's traffic carries the person's email, so Identities counts the person instead and this count of names is higher.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE api_key.id IS NOT NULL OR user.domain == "_cloud_api_key" | STATS BY api_key.id, api_key.name, user.name | EVAL key_id = COALESCE(api_key.id, user.name), kind = CASE(api_key.id IS NULL, "Cloud", "Elasticsearch"), name = COALESCE(api_key.name, user.name) | STATS `API keys` = COUNT_DISTINCT(key_id), names = COUNT_DISTINCT(name) | EVAL detail = CASE(`API keys` == 0, "none in range", names == 1, "1 name", CONCAT(CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(names)) <= 3, TO_STRING(names), LENGTH(TO_STRING(names)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(names), LENGTH(TO_STRING(names)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(names), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(names)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(names), LENGTH(TO_STRING(names)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(names), LENGTH(TO_STRING(names)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(names), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(names), LENGTH(TO_STRING(names)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(names), LENGTH(TO_STRING(names)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(names), LENGTH(TO_STRING(names)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(names), 3))), " names")) | KEEP `API keys`, detail

config.description: Events authenticated through the cloud-saml-kibana SAML realm — a person in a browser. The line under the number counts Kibana user_login events in range, or reads “signed in earlier” when there are none: the sessions behind these events began before the range, so a person can use SSO (the Humans tile) with no new sign-in here.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE user.domain == "cloud-saml-kibana" | STATS `SSO events` = COUNT(*), logins = COUNT(*) WHERE event.action == "user_login" | EVAL detail = CASE(`SSO events` == 0, "none in range", logins == 0, "signed in earlier", logins == 1, "1 new sign-in", CONCAT(CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) <= 3, TO_STRING(logins), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(logins), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(logins), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(logins), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(logins), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(logins), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(logins), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(logins), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(logins), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(logins), 3))), " new sign-ins")) | KEEP `SSO events`, detail

config.description: Failed sign-ins (authentication_failed or anonymous_access_denied, one per request; the realm_authentication_failed events Elasticsearch writes for each realm an attempt tried are left out, so an attempt counts once) plus requests refused or failed after sign-in (access_denied and any other failed outcome). The line under the number counts the failed sign-in attempts (nobody signed in: these are not logins); the rest of the number is denied — refused or failed after sign-in. A denial is an authenticated identity hitting a permission wall, not someone guessing credentials. Same predicate as the two failure panels below.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE event.action IN ("authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") OR (event.outcome == "failure" AND (event.action IS NULL OR event.action != "realm_authentication_failed")) | STATS `Failed or denied` = COUNT(*), signin = COUNT(*) WHERE event.action IN ("authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") | EVAL detail = CASE(signin == 0, "no failed sign-ins", signin == 1, "1 failed sign-in", signin == `Failed or denied`, "all failed sign-ins", CONCAT(CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) <= 3, TO_STRING(signin), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(signin), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(signin), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(signin), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(signin), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(signin), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(signin), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(signin), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(signin), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(signin), 3))), " failed sign-ins")) | KEEP `Failed or denied`, detail

config.description: Distinct Kibana browser sessions observed in range, and how many people (by email) they belong to.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE kibana.session.id IS NOT NULL | STATS `Kibana sessions` = COUNT_DISTINCT(kibana.session.id), people = COUNT_DISTINCT(user.email) | EVAL detail = CASE(`Kibana sessions` == 0, "none in range", CASE(people == 0, "no email recorded", people == 1, "1 person", CONCAT(CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) <= 3, TO_STRING(people), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(people), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(people), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(people), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(people), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(people), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(people), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(people), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(people), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(people), 3))), " people"))) | KEEP `Kibana sessions`, detail

config.title: Elasticsearch requests per minute by credential type
config.description: Elasticsearch requests per minute by how they presented credentials: API key, token (SSO browser sessions and service accounts), realm (username and password) or SAML. One bar per credential type per interval — 1 minute at 1h, 30 minutes at 24h, 3 hours at 7d — and its height is that interval's requests divided by its minutes, so the scale reads the same at every range: a lone request in a 30-minute bar is 0.033 a minute. A log scale, so a type carrying a fraction of a percent of the traffic is as readable as the bulk; an interval with no bar had no requests of that type. Every bar is a whole interval counted back from the end of the range, so the newest bar is the most recent minutes and none is left out. A shift in this mix is worth explaining.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE authentication.type IS NOT NULL | EVAL k = DATE_DIFF("second", @timestamp, TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) / CASE(DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 4500, 60, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 22500, 300, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 45000, 600, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 135000, 1800, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 270000, 3600, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 810000, 10800, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 3240000, 43200, 86400) | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY k, authentication.type | EVAL k = LEAST(k, GREATEST(DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) / CASE(DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 4500, 60, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 22500, 300, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 45000, 600, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 135000, 1800, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 270000, 3600, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 810000, 10800, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 3240000, 43200, 86400), 1) - 1) | STATS events = SUM(events) BY k, authentication.type | EVAL span = CASE(DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 4500, 60, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 22500, 300, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 45000, 600, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 135000, 1800, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 270000, 3600, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 810000, 10800, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 3240000, 43200, 86400), n = GREATEST(DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) / CASE(DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 4500, 60, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 22500, 300, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 45000, 600, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 135000, 1800, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 270000, 3600, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 810000, 10800, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) <= 3240000, 43200, 86400), 1), ts = TO_DATETIME(TO_LONG(TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) - (k + 1) * span * 1000), per_minute = events * 60.0 / (span + CASE(k == n - 1, DATE_DIFF("second", TO_DATETIME(?_tstart), TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) - n * span, 0)) | EVAL auth = CASE(authentication.type == "api_key", "API key", authentication.type == "token", "Token", authentication.type == "realm", "Realm", authentication.type == "saml", "SAML", authentication.type == "anonymous", "Anonymous", authentication.type == "internal", "Internal", authentication.type) | KEEP ts, auth, per_minute | SORT auth

config.title: Credential type by identity · Elasticsearch requests
config.description: Which credential type each of the busiest identities presents, 12 at most, and how many Elasticsearch requests it made with each: the count is printed in the cell. Cells are coloured by credential type, in the same colours as the time chart beside it, so a colour means the same thing in both panels. Humans should authenticate by token (SSO); service identities by API key. Only Elasticsearch requests record a credential type, so the counts leave out Kibana traffic and can be lower than the same identity's count in the tables below (Busiest API keys counts both), and identities seen only in Kibana or only anonymously are counted in Identities above but are not on this chart. A Cloud API key has no name and is shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key”, the first five characters of its id.

config.title: Events by identity origin
config.description: Events, not identities, by the email on the event: Elastic (@elastic.co), Tenant (any other address), or Machine (no email: service accounts, Cloud API keys, internal users and anonymous requests). Each origin's name carries its count, and the bars are on a log scale so a person's few dozen events are visible beside a key's hundreds of thousands: read the count, not the length. An origin with no bar had no events in range. One busy key can make Machine nearly all of the traffic while most identities are people. An Elasticsearch API key carries its creator's email, so traffic from a key a person created counts under that person's origin.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY user.email | EVAL actor_org = CASE(user.email IS NULL, "Machine", user.email LIKE "*@elastic.co", "Elastic", "Tenant") | STATS events = SUM(events) BY origin = actor_org | EVAL origin = CONCAT(origin, " · ", CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 3, TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)))) | SORT events DESC

config.title: Events by authentication realm
config.description: Events by the security realm that authenticated them. Each realm's name carries its count, and the bars are on a log scale so a small realm is visible beside the bulk: read the count, not the length. SAML SSO is interactive human sign-in (cloud-saml-kibana); Elasticsearch API key (_es_api_key) and Cloud API key (_cloud_api_key) are programmatic — an Elasticsearch key minted by a Cloud API key authenticates in the Cloud key's realm; Service account is Elastic's own components (_service_account). Any other realm is shown by its name. Anonymous and unauthenticated requests record no realm and are not counted, so the bars can sum to less than Events by identity origin beside it.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE user.domain IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY user.domain | EVAL realm = CASE(user.domain == "cloud-saml-kibana", "SAML SSO", user.domain == "_es_api_key", "Elasticsearch API key", user.domain == "_cloud_api_key", "Cloud API key", STARTS_WITH(user.domain, "_service_account"), "Service account", STARTS_WITH(user.domain, "_"), "Other internal", user.domain) | STATS events = SUM(events) BY realm | EVAL realm = CONCAT(realm, " · ", CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 3, TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)))) | SORT events DESC

config.title: Busiest API keys by name · top 10 at most
config.description: The busiest API keys of both kinds, one row per key name, with request volume and how many distinct client IPs used it. Kind is Cloud (an Elastic Cloud API key: it has no name and is recorded by its id, so it reads “_4KEO… · Cloud API key”, the first five characters of its id) or Elasticsearch (an Elasticsearch API key: id and name). A re-issued Elasticsearch key keeps its name under a new id, so Key IDs counts the ids a name ran under in range; API key inventory below has one row per id, with owner and first and last use. The API keys tile counts every id and every name in range, so past the ten busiest names the rows here add up to less than it; the rest are in the inventory. A key used from many IPs is worth investigating. The range ends a minute ago, so nothing in it is still arriving; each panel reads the clock for itself, up to a second apart, so two panels side by side can differ by the events of that second at either end of the range: usually none, a few on a busy all-traffic count or during a burst.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE api_key.id IS NOT NULL OR user.domain == "_cloud_api_key" | STATS events = COUNT(*), ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(client.ip), key_ids = COUNT_DISTINCT(api_key.id) BY api_key = api_key.name, user.name | EVAL kind = CASE(key_ids == 0, "Cloud", "Elasticsearch"), key_ids = GREATEST(key_ids, 1), api_key = COALESCE(api_key, CASE((LENGTH(user.name) == 20 AND user.name RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT user.name RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(user.name, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), "(no name)")) | SORT events DESC, api_key | LIMIT 10

config.title: Busiest human identities · top 10 at most
config.description: People by email, busiest first: the people the Humans tile counts, over all traffic, with the same event counts as Identity first and last seen, which also has when each was first and last seen and from how many IPs. The panel shows the top rows; the rest are in that session. Click an email to pin that person across the suite. The range ends a minute ago, so nothing in it is still arriving; each panel reads the clock for itself, up to a second apart, so two panels side by side can differ by the events of that second at either end of the range: usually none, a few on a busy all-traffic count or during a burst.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE user.email IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY user.email | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Top failed or denied access · 10 at most (empty = good)
config.description: Failed sign-ins and refused requests grouped by identity, action and source IP, most frequent first; the top rows of what the Failed or denied tile counts. Result names the kind, as in the session below: failed sign-in (authentication_failed or anonymous_access_denied, one per request; the realm_authentication_failed events Elasticsearch writes for each realm an attempt tried are left out, so an attempt counts once), denied (access_denied: an authenticated identity refused an action), or failed (any other action, here because its outcome was failure). An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. An empty panel means nothing matched in the time range, which is the healthy state; any row here is worth reading.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE event.action IN ("authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") OR (event.outcome == "failure" AND (event.action IS NULL OR event.action != "realm_authentication_failed")) | STATS events = COUNT(*), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY user.email, api_key.name, user.name, action = event.action, ip = client.ip | EVAL actor = COALESCE(user.email, api_key.name, user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS events = SUM(events), last_seen = MAX(last_seen) BY actor, action, ip | EVAL result = CASE(action IN ("authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied"), "failed sign-in", action == "access_denied", "denied", "failed"), ip = COALESCE(TO_STRING(ip), "no IP") | SORT events DESC, last_seen DESC, actor, action, ip | LIMIT 10 | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor)

config.title: Failed sign-ins and denied access · newest 1,000 at most (empty = good)
config.description: The newest failed sign-ins and refused requests, record by record. Discover stops at 1,000 rows, so on a busy range its result count is that cap and the Failed or denied tile is the total. Result names the kind: failed sign-in, denied (access_denied), or failed (any other failed outcome). Credential is the credential type, or the realm on a Kibana event, and reads “not authenticated” on a failed sign-in; Country reads “internal” for a private or carrier-NAT address, which is Kibana or the platform calling on someone's behalf. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. An empty panel means nothing matched in the time range, which is the healthy state; any row here is worth reading.

config.title: API key inventory
config.description: Every API key seen in range (up to 1,000), Cloud and Elasticsearch, busiest first — one row per key the API keys tile counts — with owner, volume, IP spread, indices touched and first and last use. Owner is the identity that created the key: a person's email, or, for a key minted programmatically, the Cloud API key that minted it, shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” like that key's own row; a Cloud API key's own creator is not in the audit stream, so its Owner reads Cloud organization.

config.title: Identity first and last seen
config.description: Every identity in range (up to 1,000), all traffic — one row per identity the Identities tile counts — with its first and last appearance, Events (everything it did, the same count as Busiest human identities) and Signal events (what is left after the noise gate, the count the gated panels across the suite use). Newest first appearance on top. Widen the time range to tell a brand-new identity from one that was simply quiet. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.
